item.title: Nettspend Honors BloodHound Q50 With “LL50” On Virginia Creeper
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Nettspend released "LL50" in memory of BloodHound Q50 on Virginia Creeper after previewing the tribute at III Points.
item.content:encoded:
Nettspend honored BloodHound Q50 with “LL50,” a memorial track released on his six-song EP Virginia Creeper, following an earlier preview at Miami’s III Points festival.

The CXO-produced song is “a tribute to Nettspend’s late friend and peer BloodHound Q50 that doubles as an ode to living life to the fullest.”

The 19-year-old rapper introduced “LL50” during his III Points appearance earlier in October and played it twice, according to the label.

The EP took its name from a vine native to Virginia, Nettspend’s home state. CXO was joined on the project’s production credits by zoot, zuro, exset, 1Deep and Che.

Before the EP, Nettspend had also linked with Che on “KickAss (Pull Up Pls)” and joined producer Evilgiane’s Boiler Room set in Los Angeles in September.

Q50, whose real name was Mikquale Cooper, was killed in Chicago on September 13. His death came more than a month before Nettspend released the tribute.

Chicago police said Q50 was in a vehicle outside a BP gas station at 4248 South Wentworth Avenue just before 4 A.M. when two other vehicles arrived and people opened fire, FOX 32 Chicago reported.

The Chicago rapper had begun making music in 2023. His early records included “Big3” and “Coffin,” and he signed with Signal Records in late 2024. He also performed at Rolling Loud in May 2026.

AllHipHop previously reported that an autopsy documented five gunshot wounds. Q50’s funeral took place September 25 in Merrillville, Indiana, where several police forces were present.

For Nettspend, the dedication followed another recent release that his label presented as a more vulnerable turn. His August 25 single “Sober” was produced by reklus1ve.

The black-and-white “Sober” video featured Nettspend’s mother and fellow rapper OsamaSon. The release preceded Virginia Creeper, which arrived later that year, along with his March debut album, early life crisis.

That 21-song debut included NBA YoungBoy and OsamaSon. The label described its subject matter as the pressures and anxiety of young adulthood, providing context for the more personal material Nettspend released ahead of “LL50.”

item.title: Plies Gets Emotional Thanking Black Women After Seeing Poll Volunteers
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Plies thanked Black women after seeing volunteers at his polling place and said he struggled to keep his emotions in check.
item.content:encoded:
Plies had a message for Black women after he voted in the midterm elections: he saw their work and wanted them to know he appreciated it.

The Florida rapper said seeing Black women volunteer at his polling place moved him. In a video shared on Instagram, he explained that he was trying to keep his emotions in check, even avoiding a direct look at the camera as he spoke.

Plies thanked Black women “for how much y’all continue to sacrifice, continue to be on the right side of history, and just continue to be amazing people.”

His defense of Black women had also shaped his support for Kamala Harris in 2024.

In an August video on X, Plies questioned why people demanded explanations from a Black woman while accepting Trump’s record. Charlamagne Tha God pushed back, saying Black voters should be able to question candidates rather than accept what they were offered.

Before the current midterms, Plies had pushed against the idea that sitting out elections carried no cost. In October, Plies used another Instagram video to question why some Black voters had lost their enthusiasm for voting.

He pointed to the excitement around Barack Obama’s presidential campaigns and argued that political opponents wanted to prevent that energy from returning. He also cited redistricting and voting restrictions while laying out his concerns about Black turnout.

Plies criticized the attacks on Kamala Harris’ racial identity during her 2024 campaign, saying they were meant to weaken support for her.

Plies described his choice at the polls as protecting his community. He said he did not tell other people how to vote and was weighing which candidate would cause the least harm.

“I’m voting for who not gon’ hurt my people the worst,” he said.

He had also addressed disappointed Harris supporters after the 2024 presidential election. After Donald Trump’s win, Plies told people who backed Harris that the result didn’t mean their beliefs were wrong.

“Just because some results didn’t go how you foreseen them to go, it doesn’t mean you wrong about anything,” Plies said.

item.title: Avalanche The Architect The Top 10 Toronto Rapper That Went From Hip Hop Veteran to International EDM Contender
item.dc:creator: Staff Writer
item.description: With 14 albums, 42 million Spotify streams, and a growing international audience, Avalanche The Architect is expanding beyond hip-hop into EDM, bringing decades of lyrical experience to dance floors worldwide.
item.content:encoded:
The numbers behind that career are substantial. According to publicly available information, Avalanche has released 14 studio albums and 48 singles, and his music has gathered more than 42 million Spotify streams and over 14 million YouTube views. That is a deep catalogue for any independent artist, and it is the foundation he is now building something new on top of.

His story starts in 1994, when he was just seven years old and already writing and performing rap. Speaking to Phoenix FM in 2024, he described coming up as a battle rapper in the Bronx before relocating to Toronto at 14. He talked about his love of nineties hip-hop and his preference for dense, intricate lyricism and high-energy performance, the values of an era when an MC earned respect by out-rapping whoever stood across from him.

That background matters, because Avalanche did not arrive in electronic music as a bedroom producer chasing a trend. He came to it with decades of studio and stage experience already behind him, and you can hear that confidence in the way he has approached the genre.

The clearest example is “Booty Fat (Big Butts Don’t Lie),” released as part of his 2025 Booty Fat Radio Remix project. The title tells you exactly what kind of record it is: playful, unapologetic and built for the club. Rather than treating it as a one-off, he followed it with “Big Butts Don’t Lie (Extended EDM Mix),” a longer version shaped for DJs and dance-floor audiences, and both now sit in his Apple Music catalogue. Tracks such as “Techno Booty” and “Electronic Dance Money” push the same idea further, showing that the electronic side of his work is a sustained direction rather than a single experiment.

What makes the shift interesting is the contrast. The same artist who spent decades sharpening his craft as a lyricist is now working in a genre with an entirely different production vocabulary, one built on repetition, build-ups and drops rather than bars and punchlines. It is a risk that many veteran rappers would not take, and it has opened his music up to listeners who might never have come across his hip-hop records.

The international reach of that catalogue is where the story gets most surprising. Spotify chart records compiled by the tracking site Kworb show his recordings registering chart activity across a wide spread of markets. “Electronic Dance Money” alone has picked up chart positions in Ukraine, Hong Kong, the United Arab Emirates, Bolivia, Lithuania, Belarus, Latvia and Estonia. Other records show chart activity for his music in France, Canada and South Africa, with Luxembourg and Iceland also appearing in his chart history.

Taken together, that is a footprint stretching across Europe, North America, South America, Asia, the Middle East and Africa. For an independent artist working outside the major-label system, without a global marketing machine behind him, that kind of spread is notable. It suggests his electronic records are finding listeners on their own terms, travelling through playlists and dance floors in places he has never toured.

It also says something about how music moves in 2026. A track no longer needs radio or a big-budget rollout to find an audience in Vilnius, Dubai or Johannesburg. What it needs is a sound that connects, and Avalanche’s club records, with their straightforward energy and bold hooks, appear to be doing exactly that.

None of this means he has left hip-hop behind. His catalogue still reflects the rapper who started out in the battle circuit, and his move into EDM reads less like a reinvention than an expansion: another room added to a house he has been building for more than three decades. The name fits. The Architect has always been about construction, and his latest work shows he is still drawing up new plans.

From a seven-year-old writing rhymes in 1994 to an artist charting in markets on almost every continent, Avalanche The Architect’s career has rarely followed a straight line. If his recent run is any indication, the next chapter will not either.

Official website: www.avalanchethearchitect.com

item.title: Spike Lee Urges Knicks To Skip Trump White House Visit
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Spike Lee said he hoped the Knicks would skip a Trump White House visit, months after owner James Dolan accepted an invitation.
item.content:encoded:
Spike Lee said he hoped the New York Knicks would skip a White House visit with Donald Trump. The film director and courtside fixture took a stand against a trip owner James Dolan wanted.

Stephen A. Smith had raised the issue last week. He claimed Dolan was upset because Knicks players did not want to go. But Smith cautioned, “I don’t know whether this is true or not.”

“He can’t force them!” Lee told Variety. “It’s been years since the last NBA team has gone. They’re not going. I hope they don’t go!”

Dolan had accepted the White House invitation in June, soon after the Knicks won the NBA title. He broke that news on WFAN on June 17. At the time, he said the details still had to be worked out. The Knicks became the first NBA champs to accept a White House trip during Trump’s current term.

“He is a friend. I’ve known him for 30 years and I’m very proud to bring the team to the White House,” Dolan said.

That friendship had already been on display during the Finals. Dolan invited Trump to Game 3 at Madison Square Garden. Trump went to the game and praised both the owner and the team.

The June announcement left a key question open: Would the full roster go? Dolan had accepted for the team, but the players had not made their own views on the trip public at that point.

NBA champs had passed on White House trips during Trump’s first term. Golden State stayed away after its 2017 and 2018 titles amid the dispute between Stephen Curry and Trump. Toronto did not make the trip after its 2019 win.

The Boston Celtics were the last NBA team to visit the White House, in 2024. Oklahoma City did not go after its 2025 title, citing timing and scheduling issues.

The Knicks had yet to decide on a White House visit as of September 29, according to a Reuters report.

In September, coach Mike Brown said the team was still “internally discussing” whether to go.

The Knicks had yet to decide as of Lee’s interview.

item.title: Yung Miami’s “MLK” Birthday Request Is Hilarious From TikTok Michael Jackson
item.dc:creator: illseed
item.description: Yung Miami’s request for the “Martin Luther King version” of “Happy Birthday” gave Looze Cannon comedy material.
item.content:encoded:
Yung Miami’s “Martin Luther King” Birthday Request Has Me Cracking Up

Hold on! Yung Miami is a shapeshifter to me. Sometimes I’m looking right at her and don’t immediately realize it’s Caresha. One minute, she’s giving celebrity. The next, she looks like somebody I might run into around the way. I don’t mean that negatively, either. Sometimes she just looks familiar.

I’m going somewhere with this.

Recently, I saw a clip of her talking to Looze Cannon, the entertainer doing those hilarious Michael Jackson impressions on TikTok. You know who I’m talking about. Big Michael Michael!

Anyway, Caresha wanted him to sing “Happy Birthday” to her. But she had a particular version in mind. She wanted the “Martin Luther King version.”

Now, hold on! The Martin Luther King version?!

Looze Cannon caught on quickly. She meant Stevie Wonder’s “Happy Birthday,” the one a lot of us immediately recognize once that chorus gets going.

The way she described it, followed by his reaction, was enough for me. Sometimes the funniest moments happen when somebody is being completely serious.

Big Michael Michael caught on quickly. She meant Stevie Wonder’s “Happy Birthday.” Now, I have never, ever in my long-legged life heard somebody think Dr. King sang a birthday song. MLK on lead vocals is different! Caresha is not the sharpest knife in the kitchen.

And yet that’s where Looze Cannon comes in. His reaction and timing made the whole thing funnier. Sometimes you don’t have to write a joke. Somebody hands you the material, and you just have to know what to do with it. He did that.

She took the scenic route to Stevie Wonder, but she got us there. LOL! TF!

Now, let’s talk about Looze Cannon. This man is funny enough that I hope he has the right people helping him turn this attention into something sustainable. His official website identifies him as a recording artist, streamer, producer, DJ and comedic personality. That explains why he seems so comfortable mixing music with whatever foolishness happens on a livestream.

I know he raps, but I can also see him doing more comedy. The timing, the reactions, the ability to take somebody else’s unexpected comment and run with it. There’s something there.

And Caresha gave him something to work with.

The comments I saw were not letting her live, either. I won’t call her stupid over this one. You can,but I won’t. We can laugh at this and keep it pushing.

Here is some history for the people.

Stevie Wonder released “Happy Birthday” on his 1980 album Hotter Than July, using music to rally support for a federal holiday honoring Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. I did not realize it was THAT long ago. The album also included an appeal asking listeners to support the effort of making the King’s birthday into law. Wonder joined a broader movement that included Coretta Scott King and lawmakers pushing for recognition. The first federal observance of Martin Luther King Jr. Day took place in January 1986. That familiar birthday chorus carries a civil rights legacy. I hope Caresha’s reading this.

Watch the clip above and tell me what you think in the comments.

Let’s jam to Big Michael Michael!

item.title: Blac Chyna Faces $116K California Tax Lien Tied To 2024
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Blac Chyna faced a $116,732.37 California state tax lien tied to 2024 as her child-support history drew new attention.
item.content:encoded:
Blac Chyna is facing a $116,732.37 California state tax lien tied to the 2024 tax year, according to Page Six.

The California Franchise Tax Board filed it against Angela White, the model and reality star known as Blac Chyna.

The filing leaves one key question open: White’s response. The available report does not say whether she disputes the balance or how she plans to address it.

California’s Franchise Tax Board says unpaid state tax debt creates a statutory lien. The lien attaches to a taxpayer’s real or personal property. The agency says a recorded Notice of State Tax Lien may also become public.

A state tax lien is not a criminal conviction, and this filing does not prove White is broadly insolvent.

The child-support history in the report adds context, but it is separate from the tax claim. Rob Kardashian agreed in 2017 to pay White $20,000 per month. A 2019 agreement later ended payments in either direction. Each parent was to cover their child’s costs during their own parenting time.

The 2019 deal marked a clear shift from the 2017 arrangement. It did not mean parenting became cost-free. It changed how they handled expenses by tying costs to each parent’s time with their child.

White spoke about the arrangement and said raising her children without support her “biggest flex.”

The comment did not go unchallenged. AllHipHop reported in 2022 that Tyga and Kardashian disputed her no-support account.

The family picture kept changing. By 2024, People reported that White had 50/50 custody of both children. That detail updates the history around her parenting agreements. It does not explain or settle California’s reported tax claim for 2024.

The two issues can get blurred because the lien story arrived with years of child-support headlines. They are still different matters. The old support debate centered on how White and the fathers handled expenses for their children. The new filing concerns a specific state tax balance tied to White.

For now, White’s position remains the clearest open point. Her representative had not immediately commented on the reported $116,732.37 lien.

item.title: Nicki Minaj Loses Again After Kathy Hochul Re-Elected As NY Governor
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Kathy Hochul won another term as New York governor after Nicki Minaj urged Black and Christian voters to back Bruce Blakeman.
item.content:encoded:
Kathy Hochul won another term as New York governor on November 3, defeating Bruce Blakeman after Nicki Minaj urged Black and Christian voters to back his campaign. The Associated Press called the race for Hochul.

Blakeman conceded Tuesday night and said he had spoken with Hochul. He said, “we all have to unify and work together.”

Minaj backed Blakeman on October 28 with an appeal aimed at Black and Christian voters. Her criticism of Hochul brought an older controversy back into the campaign: the governor’s remarks about Black children in the Bronx and their familiarity with computers.

Hochul made that comment on May 6, 2024. She apologized that day, said she had misspoken and explained that she meant to address barriers to access. The remark had also drawn criticism from 50 Cent in 2024, during that earlier dispute.

“Kathy Hochul is an evil woman,” Minaj wrote in her October 28 post. The rapper also accused the governor of failing to condemn wrongdoing, taking her criticism beyond an appeal to vote for the other candidate.

Asked about Minaj during a campaign stop in Albany, Hochul told her to spend less time online. “And stop going to Trump rallies because it’s poisoning your mind,” the governor said.

Minaj had appeared at a Donald Trump rally in Michigan earlier that week and urged young voters to support Republicans. Her backing for Blakeman was part of that broader push as voters prepared to choose candidates in the midterm elections.

Blakeman joined the exchange himself, joking on social media that he had a moving truck ready for Hochul. His campaign continued its statewide tour in the closing days of the race.

The dispute also reached “The Breakfast Club.” On October 29, Charlamagne Tha God questioned Minaj’s moral reasoning for attacking Hochul. “That’s selective outrage, if you ask me,” he said.

Hochul first became governor in August 2021 after Andrew Cuomo resigned and won her first full term in 2022. Her running mate, former New York City Council Speaker Adrienne Adams, became the first Black woman elected lieutenant governor. New York elected women to both jobs together for the first time.

item.title: Tinashe Tells Republican Fans “Yall Can Go” Over Election Day Backlash
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Tinashe told Republican critics they could leave after her blue-heart Election Day message drew complaints from conservative fans.
item.content:encoded:
Tinashe made it clear that keeping Republican listeners was not more important than saying where she stood on Election Day.

The singer opened with a blunt get-out-the-vote post on X. “VOTE OR DIE ! LETS GO AMERICA,” she wrote, followed by 12 blue hearts. The hearts appeared to signal support for Democrats, and some conservative followers immediately objected.

One critic accused her of refusing to listen to supporters and asked why she included blue hearts. The user also said she was alienating her “red audience.” Tinashe did not soften the message. “Yall can go ✌️,” she replied.

That exchange went further than a routine voting reminder.

Tinashe was responding directly to the idea that an artist should avoid partisan politics so fans on the other side will keep listening. When another user dismissed the election as an illusion, she answered with a simple “Lame !!!!”

Her position is not new. Before the 2020 presidential election, Tinashe told Pitchfork that another Trump term would harm groups his administration had failed to protect. She closed that statement with: “Vote for Joe Biden, period.”

On Election Day that year, she also appeared at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, as the venue served as a vote center. Tinashe told ABC7 Los Angeles that she wanted to “encourage my fans to come vote” and get young people involved.

This year’s dispute came as Tinashe enjoys a major run in her independent career.

Her album Popstar was released September 25 and became her first Top 10 album on the Billboard 200. AllHipHop reported that it debuted at No. 6, well above the No. 17 peak of her 2014 album Aquarius.

She also announced an 18-stop North American tour that starts April 14, 2027, in Dallas. The tour followed three sold-out “3 Nights With A Popstar” dates in Chicago, Brooklyn and Los Angeles. That momentum gave fresh weight to complaints about what Republican customers had spent on her music.

Politics also appears in Tinashe’s recent work. On “Crash Out,” she sings, “The American dream is outdated.”

In an October profile, she said the country is balancing that dream against the reality many people live.

One critic told Tinashe that Republican fans had supported her financially even when they disagreed with her politics. The user said those listeners respected her, accused her of telling them to leave and announced that they would stop listening.

Tinashe’s answer was four words long: “I do not care.”

item.title: Nicki Minaj Hit & Missed On The Campaign Trail, But What Happens To Her Hip-Hop Legacy?
item.dc:creator: Chuck Creekmur (@ChuckCreekmur)
item.description: Nicki Minaj’s Election Day appearance in New Hampshire has her political choices colliding with her Hip-Hop legacy.
item.content:encoded:
Nicki Minaj jumped out there on the campaign trail! And as somebody who supported her at one point, albeit a very long time ago, I have to say this plainly: I feel her trash cannot be recycled.

She decided to switch sides. What you consider a “side” is your business, but my disappointment feels personal. Right now, I won’t be forgiving this particular chapter. Ever.

Now, let’s get to it.

Nicki became an amplifier of Donald Trump’s messaging, and she showed up in New Hampshire on Election Day. NBC Boston reported that she appeared outside the polling station at Pinkerton Academy in Derry around 5:30 p.m. Tuesday, November 3. She greeted people, posed for pictures and eventually boarded an unmarked tour bus after police escorted her away. Oh yeah, she shook a hand. That woman thanked her for touring with the president. Nicki’s response? “My pleasure.”

My pleasure? Well, watching this has certainly not been mine.

Her appearance also brought an obvious question back into the conversation: Can Nicki herself vote?

Here is what we can actually say. Nicki publicly said in 2024 that she was not a U.S. citizen. In January 2026, she said she was finalizing citizenship paperwork. Recent reporting has not established that she completed that process, so her current citizenship and voting eligibility remain unconfirmed. I am certain she’s still ineligible. The hypocrisy of it all…

I am pretty positive she would make a citizenship announcement a major moment. Anyway…

My issue is the choice she has made with her platform and the way they presented her.

The Nicki many of us came up loving was a tremendous talent with personality, humor and an ability to make Hip-Hop feel unpredictable. Her connection with LGBTQ+ audiences was part of that story, too. Out featured her on its cover in 2010, long before this current political chapter. And that shape-shifting is part of her brand.

This reptilian creature that looks like a “They Live” extra is not. Now I’m watching her promote a political movement I strongly oppose – MAGA. To me, the whole thing is the Empire in Star Wars attempting to come to life. Somebody tell the X-wing fighters where the Death Star is.

So, yes, I understand why people would clown this pivot. I have jokes myself. But underneath the jokes is severe, unmitigated disappointment. I supported the artist at a point, and I don’t like what she has become. It happens far too often these days.

The bigger question is what happens next.

Has she permanently damaged her relationship with Hip-Hop? In my eyes, she has done mortal damage. I’m thinking fewer listeners, weaker ticket sales and a smaller audience is what’s left. I have seen with my own eyes die-hards depart realizing the Barbz are essentially another cult.

Here is something we can say for certain.

Celebrity does not automatically delivers votes. A crowd, a photo opportunity and a bus do not tell us how anybody voted. Nicki’s actual influence did not do what they wanted to happen. It did not shave off Black, Brown and youth votes from the Dems. That was the play the first time O.G. (Orange Gangster) got elected and know this as a fact. This time, however, I did not have rappers and other rap influencers admitting to MAGA meetings. This time, it seems, they switched the strategy for one big fish like MAGA Minaj.

Could she move further into political commentary or streaming? I can imagine it. She still has fiercely loyal supporters, and some will follow her wherever she goes. I mean, again, are these loyalists even politically minded? I do not know.

The disdain for this political turn is nobody’s secret. At this point, I would welcome a break from the campaign appearances. I miss being able to discuss Nicki without feeling like I have wandered into a Trump rally.

Before I depart, Reecie Colbert, the fiery radio host and talking head, did a great job of articulating how many feel about Nicki Minaj.

Oh and this was hilarious.

Nicki Minaj – at one point – built anticipation through guest verses, animated, distorted characters and a delivery that could change within a single bar. MAGA Minaj has applied the same cartoonish personality to her adulation for The Donald, MAGA and her Extreme Right constituents. Imagine the Nicki we supported standing on command after an accused “everything” tells her. Meh.

Wherever you are, stay there.

What do you think? Share your thoughts in the comments.

item.title: Maxxing Wins Word Of The Year But Hip-Hop Knows A Different Meaning
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Maxxing takes Dictionary.com’s 2026 crown, while Will Smith and Big L show how an older form meant taking it easy in Hip-Hop.
item.content:encoded:
Maxxing earned Dictionary.com’s 2026 Word of the Year honor as the push to get more from daily life became a trend with its own language.

The pick covers a form of self-improvement that can turn meals, looks or even nights on the couch into goals to pursue.

Dictionary.com announced its choice as the term spread beyond longer words and came to be used as a verb on its own.

Looksmaxxing focuses on appearance, while tokenmaxxing describes efforts to use AI as much as possible at work.

Some uses are jokes about that pressure, with cozymaxxing giving a quiet evening at home the language of a grand pursuit.

“Maxxing is the linguistic manifestation of a culture increasingly preoccupied with getting the most out of everything,” Dictionary Media Group’s Steve Johnson said.

The company’s research found that August’s digital media use of maxxing was nearly 19 times the monthly average recorded in 2025.

The other finalists were affordability, data center, odyssey and unc, a field that mixed money worries with tech and slang.

Its account traces the newer form through gaming’s min-maxing strategy, where players build strengths that can offset a character’s weak points.

Rap listeners have another reason to recognize the sound, though the meaning they heard years ago went in a different direction.

Will Smith used “maxin'” in the theme for The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air, which began airing in 1990. He performed the theme as the Fresh Prince, with DJ Jazzy Jeff producing the song that introduced the sitcom.

“Chillin’ out, maxin’, relaxin’ all cool,” Smith rapped as the song set up his character’s move from Philadelphia to Bel-Air.

That older use meant taking it easy, a sense also preserved in Dictionary.com’s entry for “max out”, which includes “Relax, take things easy.”

Big L made the meaning plain on “Ebonics (Criminal Slang),” his 1998 underground single that translated street terms through a series of rhymed definitions.

While the newer spelling often points toward doing more, the Harlem rapper’s definition on “Ebonics” was just four words: “Max mean to relax.”

The two rap examples establish decades of use for the older form without proving that today’s online trend came from either record.
